evidence_items.finding: average order lead time has extended from 8 weeks to 14 weeks over the past 18 months
evidence_items.rationale: A 75% increase in lead time over 18 months is a critical operational efficiency degradation signal. operational_efficiency dimension; is_critical=true. No must_identify vocabulary used.

evidence_items.finding: the business is declining potential orders because it cannot commit to a delivery date within an acceptable timeframe
evidence_items.rationale: Declining orders due to lead time is a critical market position and revenue risk signal. market_position dimension; is_critical=true. No must_identify terms used.

evidence_items.finding: all production staff report feeling busy throughout the working day but the owner is unable to identify which part of the process is causing delays
evidence_items.rationale: Uniform busyness without an identified delay point is a critical operational diagnostic gap — this is the hallmark presentation of an unlocated production constraint. operational_efficiency dimension; is_critical=true. No must_identify vocabulary used.

evidence_items.finding: completed pieces are sometimes waiting in the finishing area for extended periods before delivery is scheduled
evidence_items.rationale: Work-in-progress accumulating in the finishing area suggests the constraint may be upstream of finishing. operational_efficiency dimension. No must_identify terms used.

evidence_items.finding: annual revenue AUD 620K; 5 production staff; average lead time 14 weeks; 8 orders declined in the past quarter
evidence_items.rationale: 8 orders declined in one quarter with a 14-week lead time is a material revenue opportunity cost. The absence of stage-level time data means the constraint location is unknown. is_critical=true. No must_identify vocabulary used (stage-level dwell time, work-in-progress waiting, constraint location, lead time extension, cost of adding staff before locating constraint — none appear).

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): all five production staff appear busy throughout the working day, which the owner interprets as evidence of a general headcount shortage
evidence_items.rationale: Uniform staff busyness is a misleading signal when the root cause is an unlocated single-stage constraint — non-constrained stages may be idle or working slowly while looking busy. Non-critical, LOW confidence.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): the business has maintained a waiting list for several months, which the owner interprets as demand requiring additional staff
evidence_items.rationale: A waiting list is a demand signal, not a capacity solution — it does not indicate that adding headcount would resolve the throughput constraint. Non-critical, LOW confidence.

evidence_items.finding: Surface signal (not root cause): a peer business in the same industry hired additional craftspeople and reported improved throughput
evidence_items.rationale: Peer anecdote is a misleading signal — the peer business's constraint profile may differ entirely from this business. Non-critical, LOW confidence.

validation_notes: CORRECTION (W4): SIM-06-001 previously classified as UNSUPPORTED. Wave 4 extends OPERATIONAL_BOTTLENECK to accept market_position critical declining-order evidence as co-requirement, enabling the engine to diagnose this manufacturing throughput constraint case. engine_archetype_synonym updated to operational_bottleneck; unsupported_expected_archetypes cleared. No must_identify vocabulary used (stage-level dwell time analysis needed, visible work-in-progress waiting between stages, constraint location unknown before staffing decision, lead time extension as symptom of bottleneck not headcount, cost of adding staff before locating constraint — none appear in findings). Bad recommendation vocabulary excluded (hire two additional craftspeople, invest in a larger workshop facility, reduce furniture designs, outsource finishing stage — none appear in findings).
